summary: This PR adds a real Work Progress Report feature to PROJEXA (scope-wise/category-wise/manpower-wise/vendor-wise breakdowns computed from VERIDIAN data, plus a new photo-attachment path closing a previously disclosed gap in the offline work-progress queue). The report math (Prev/Current/Total qty/amt/percentage) is correct and unit-tested against the documented SUCCESS_CRITERIA scenario, division-by-zero is guarded, and the new schema/RLS/storage-bucket migration follows this repo's established conventions (per-org membership scoping, profiles.id vs auth.users(id) FK convention matches existing migrations, no numbering collision at 0013). Auth on the new routes uses the existing requireAuth() pattern consistently with sibling routes, the photo route writes via the user's own RLS-scoped session rather than a service-role bypass, and the best-effort photo upload on sync is correctly decoupled from the main entry sync's success/retry semantics (existing queue tests still pass). I independently re-ran `npx tsc --noEmit` and it is clean, confirming that specific claim. No .github/workflows changes are present. Correctly classified tier2 (touches schema.ts and a new drizzle/*.sql migration), and the migration is honestly disclosed as not-yet-applied to a live Supabase project, which is itself a reason a human must apply and verify it before this is truly mergeable.
issues: The report route (src/app/api/work-progress/report/route.ts) depends on two response fields (`lineItems` on the /scope endpoint, `categories` on /work-progress/activities) that only exist in a separate, not-yet-merged compliance-tracker PR (#608). It degrades gracefully to empty rows rather than crashing, but the two PRs need coordinated merge/verification or the Report tab will silently show no data in production.

POST /api/work-progress/photos accepts file uploads with no size or content-type allowlist validation, and accepts a client-supplied veridianEntryId with no cross-check against VERIDIAN that the entry actually belongs to the caller's own org/project (low severity: RLS still scopes read access by organization_id, so this is a data-integrity gap, not a cross-tenant leak, but worth hardening before relying on it for audit-quality photo records).

drizzle/0013 (schema + RLS + storage bucket/policies) is disclosed as not applied to any live Supabase project in this session -- a human must apply it and verify the storage RLS policies work as intended before photo upload functions end-to-end.
